newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end sharply lower in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end sharply lower in profit-taking.

text.p: Chilean blue chips skidded to close over one percent softer in thin trade as the market hit a bout of profit-taking but stocks are expected to regain their footing Tuesday, said dealers.
"We should see the bolsa starting to stabilize in the next couple of days," said one broker.
"The thin volume shows there wasn't any serious selling."
The 40-share IPSA index ended down 1.23 percent at 114.54 points.
The general IGPA index lost 0.84 percent to 5,323.42 points amid turnover of 6.3 billion pesis.
Traders said the slump was a correction following the sharp rise in stock prices since New Year, but the thin selling indicated that demand remains strong among foreign investors.
Investors reacted negatively to fourth quarter earnings which were lower than expectations, said traders.
"Earnings don't look good, especially when you consider how high prices have risen," said one trader.
Results which disappointed the market included copper products maker Madeco whose earnings fell last year to 9.13 billion pesos from 20.18 billion pesos in 1995.
Madeco ended down 0.81 percent at 1,180-2/5 pesos.
Other losers included telecom Telex, down 4.84 percent at 1,180 pesos and forestry firm Masisa which declined 4.46 percent to 225 pesos.
Winners included winery Santa Emiliana, up 1.8 percent at 51 pesos and glass-maker Cristales which rose 0.17 percent at 2,975 pesos.
